questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many different things - the university and the classes that were available, but also the social life of the faculty.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes very.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy through university

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Long transport time. Outside city center... But cheap! Good student community in dorms! :-)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was cheap. For a reason! I would say pretty old and grimey (Charles Dorms Vetrnik).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration through SIS (online portal) and then going to the erasmus office afterwards to get them approved. I had no issues, but I know other people who struggled a bit...

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus office open twice a week, could also email them. Also student organization for Science Faculty at Charles could help I think.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have a couple weeks to try out the classes you're interested in - sign up for more classes, try them out and then drop them if you want. Sometimes the workload and ETCS does not make sense... But mostly it is fine!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All classes were very easy to pass, exams were easy compared to home university. I liked it but I know some other people wished it was more challenging! But then choose more MA classes if you are a bachelors student.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some MA and some BA, a good mix. No problems following along.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less participation, less work during the classes in general. Often you sit down and listen (or not). But I had some really passionate and good professors!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental Informatics, Human Geography Research of Czechia II, Selected Chapters from Physical Geography and Geoecology, Quaternary Palaeoenvironments, Ice Sheets and Glaciers in the Warming World, Natural Hazards and Risks, R and Python in Geosciences.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you want an exchange, where the focus is not too academically challenging, so you can engage in other aspects of the exchange: 
- Environmental Informatics
- Ice Sheets and Glaciers in the Warming World
- Selected Chapters from Physical Geography and Geoecology

If you want something with a more challenging exam and more coursework: 
- Natural Hazards and Risks (some people said the exam was the most challenging one they had had at Charles)
- R and Python in Geosciences (more coursework, but easy if you're ok with coding)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: - I don't think I experienced any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
- Eating out and going out is cheap.
- Public transportation is VERY cheap. 100kr for 3 months...
- Food in the grocery stores is cheaper - but some prices are similar (eggs, meat etc.)
- If you want to find an apartment or room be prepared to spend money. You can be lucky, but some people end up spending 4000.00kr for a room in a shared apartmet... Also beware of scams!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus club hosted events all the time. Easter events, quiz nights... you name it!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join karaoke, and the cultural events! Try to go to as many as you have the energy for at the start of the semester. :-)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel in surrounding countries with people from uni

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't do much of that

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hiking culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- The beer is cheap
- The lectures are going to be a little different from what you are used to in my opinion - but enjoy the experience!
- Try to learn some of the language. If possible, sign up for the in-person language course!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Connecting with other international students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting a doctors appointment while being sick... But you can, I just had back luck! Other people did it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
